label: Groovy field
title: When can the Groovy field run on its own? A full-line census
summary: A bounded full-line census reports 140 elementary-rule Groovy fields closing with one to four remembered fields. Independent replay confirms Rule 30 at memory three and Rule 54 at five; source gradients with two-step histories repair all 256 in the census.
takeaway: A repair can make G autonomous while identifying at most complementary sources. Uniform sources stay merged, but other complement pairs can be separated. Native Groovy iteration of a repaired law requires off-image dynamics.

label: Groovy geometry
title: Three Groovy rows need their temporal seam
summary: An eleven-cell periodic Rule-30 source gives identical unlabelled three-row input planes requiring different successors. No uniform binary 2D rule can advance this period-three encoding at one-step cadence, at any radius.
takeaway: Ordered memory-three autonomy survives. Spatially arranging the raw bits and forgetting their temporal roles is a further information loss; markers, boundaries or another encoding remain possible.

label: Groovy separator
title: One extra binary row makes the Groovy history spatial
summary: Either a zero or a one separator repairs the three-row Rule-30 Groovy history as a uniform binary 2D CA on a 13-by-4 stencil. The complete 21-bit source cone and all four phases are checked independently.
takeaway: G never contains 1111, so a ones row is a local marker. A zero separator also closes: unique temporal labels are unnecessary when ambiguous readings agree on the successor. The extra row and local access have explicit costs.
